articles_note: english glues no article to a headword, but the vocabulary list carries the infinitive marker on every verb, and a verb left carrying it is a verb no dictionary answers to
audio_note: the backup ships real recordings for most of the deck, so little reaches wiktionary and less still reaches synthesis
inflection_note: english wiktionary states a verb's forms in its headword line rather than in a conjugation table, so the inflection stage has nothing to read and is left off

graded_lexicon.name: efllex
graded_lexicon.note: records where a word appears in graded material, not where it is taught, and is keyed on the headword while cards are keyed on the sense — a floor, not a verdict

deck_note: named for the levels it holds, since the finished ones live in their own deck
mastered_levels_note: levels the learner has finished; their cards stay suspended, and re-levelling keeps refilling them, so they are hidden again after every push
mastered_deck_note: finished levels live outside the main deck, so studying it only ever reaches the levels still being learned
card_templates_note: the learner already reads english, so producing a word from its meaning is not what the deck is for; a word is met either inside a sentence or on its own
superseded_cards_note: a word met inside a sentence has already been asked what it means, so the bare headword card stands down for it; a word with no sentence keeps it
